tracks.title: Slide Fourteen
tracks.mood: sheepish, grateful and smiling at himself
tracks.subject: running the lyric slides at a Sunday service and always being one line behind the band
tracks.caption: Christian worship-pop in the bouncy 2025 CCM-crossover style. A bright strummed steel-string acoustic guitar with a ukulele doubling the chords; a lo-fi hip-hop drum loop with a swung kick, a soft snare dusted with vinyl crackle and finger snaps on two and four; a clean Rhodes electric piano holding warm seventh chords; a round electric bass playing short notes; a unison congregation gang vocal arriving on the last chorus. Close and warm, narrow low end, the acoustic guitar and lead voice forward, a light room sound on the gang vocal. Male voice, an earnest, clear light baritone, half-rapping the verses in a relaxed conversational flow and singing the chorus straight. 100 BPM, G major. Sheepish, grateful and smiling at himself. No gospel choir or Hammond organ, no soul melisma, no ambient worship pads or dotted-eighth delay guitar, no slow stadium build, no trap hi-hat rolls, no autotune, no EDM drop.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - strummed acoustic guitar and finger snaps]

[Verse 1]
Nine-fifteen on Sunday, I'm up in the booth with the laptop
Pastor Dave gave me the clicker when Kyle moved to Phoenix
Band's already on the second verse and I'm still on the title
Three hundred people looking up at a blank blue screen

[Pre-Chorus]
I hit the arrow twice, now it's last week's song
Mrs Alvarez sings it right without me

[Chorus]
I'm a line behind, I'm a line behind
Every Sunday morning I'm a line behind
And they sing it anyway, they don't even look up
Slide fourteen, I'm still catching up

[Verse 2]
Week four, somebody typed the bridge and spelled Lord as Lard
A kid in row three laughs till his mom gives him the look
I'm sweating in the booth with my finger on backspace
And the room just sings right over the typo

[Pre-Chorus]
Then the bulb in the projector pops
And nobody needs me at all

[Chorus - gang vocals enter]
I'm a line behind, I'm a line behind
Every Sunday morning I'm a line behind
And they sing it in the dark, every single word
Slide fourteen, and I'm singing too

[Bridge - Rhodes and finger snaps only]
Lights come up on the last amen
And I'm standing in the booth with both hands up

[Outro - acoustic guitar alone]
Pastor Dave says keep the clicker
I say only if the bulb blows again

tracks.title: Gate Forty-One
tracks.mood: flirty and unhurried, hoping the delay gets longer
tracks.subject: sharing one phone charger with a stranger at an airport gate during a five-hour delay
tracks.caption: Amapiano pop in the 2025 South African crossover style. A pitched log-drum bass that glides between notes and plays the whole bassline; a sparse kick that skips beats; shakers and syncopated open hi-hats carrying the groove; jazzy Rhodes chords in extended ninth voicings; a soft airy pad underneath. Dry and spacious with lots of air between the parts, the log drum and the voice forward. Female voice, breathy and laid-back R&B in the low-middle register, singing close to the mic, with her own soft harmony doubling the hook lines. 112 BPM, F minor. Flirty and unhurried, hoping the delay gets longer. No four-on-the-floor house kick, no afrobeats guitar, no trap hi-hats, no autotune, no sampled voice hooks, no EDM drop.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - log drum and Rhodes chords, short]

[Verse 1]
Gate forty-one and the board just turned red
Delayed till ten and my phone's on four percent
One plug by the window and you're sat on it
You hold up your cable and say we can take turns

[Pre-Chorus]
Twenty minutes yours, twenty minutes mine
You set a timer on your watch

[Chorus]
Don't board it yet, don't board it yet
I've got your charger and you've got half my fries
Twenty minutes yours, twenty minutes mine
Don't board it yet

[Verse 2]
Same flight, you're nine C and I'm thirty-two E
You say the middle seat next to you is free
The screen says delayed again till twelve
And I don't even sigh

[Pre-Chorus]
Your timer's gone off three times now
Neither of us moved the plug

[Chorus]
Don't board it yet, don't board it yet
I've got your charger and I've got your coat
Row nine, middle seat, if they'll let me move
Don't board it yet

[Instrumental Break - log drum solo with shakers]

[Outro - log drum alone, then Rhodes]
Now boarding, gate forty-one
You say keep the cable, see you in row nine

tracks.title: Spare Key
tracks.mood: giddy, out of breath, happily in love
tracks.subject: getting a spare key cut for your partner at the key kiosk under the stairs at Waterloo station
tracks.caption: UK pop drum and bass in the current festival style. A clean, tightly quantized two-step drum and bass beat with a kick on one and on the and of three, a sharp layered snare on two and four, and ghost-note hi-hats; a rolling sub bass in the verses that turns into a growling detuned Reese bass for the drop; euphoric piano stabs on the off-beats; wide supersaw chords building through a riser and a white-noise sweep into the drop. Clean and wide, the sub and snare forward, the piano bright and close. Female voice, a clear pop soprano, close and conversational in the verses, open and full in the chorus. 174 BPM, E minor. Giddy, out of breath, happily in love. No chopped Amen breaks, no ragga voice, no trap hi-hats, no autotune, no dubstep wobble, no sampled voice hooks.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - piano stabs and rolling sub, short]

[Verse 1]
Key kiosk under the stairs at Waterloo
Man with a grinder and a radio on
I hand him mine and he says just the one?
I say just the one, and I go red

[Pre-Chorus]
Sparks off the wheel and my heart's going
Eight pound fifty, I tap my card twice

[Chorus]
It's a spare key, it's a spare key
Brass and still warm in my hand
Second on the left when you get to the top
You don't have to knock again

[Drop - growling Reese bass and full drums, no vocals]

[Verse 2]
I put it on a ring with a plastic lemon
So you'll find it at the bottom of your bag
Practised what to say on the Northern line
Then I just said here, and you just said oh

[Pre-Chorus]
You tried it in the door that night
Jiggle it left, it sticks a bit

[Chorus]
It's a spare key, it's a spare key
Brass and still warm in your hand
Second on the left when you get to the top
You don't ever have to knock again

[Drop - growling Reese bass and full drums, no vocals]

[Outro - piano alone after the drop, then the sub cuts out]
Came home Thursday and the lights were on
You'd let yourself in

tracks.title: Name On The Lid
tracks.mood: sassy, accusatory and danceable
tracks.subject: four flatmates interrogating each other over a strawberry yoghurt with a name written on the lid
tracks.caption: Global girl-group pop in the current K-pop-system style, sung in English. A punchy 808 kick with tight hi-hat rolls only under the rap verse; Latin-pop nylon-string guitar flourishes between the lines; stacked synth-brass stabs announcing each chorus; a dance break with a hard beat switch to half-time; the last chorus lifting up a key. Glossy and wide, the drums and stacked voices forward, the nylon guitar close and dry. Four young female voices trading lines: a bright lead soprano, a cool low alto, a quick spoken-rap verse, unison group chants on the hook, and one belted high note in the bridge. 118 BPM, C-sharp minor. Sassy, accusatory and danceable. No autotune, no EDM supersaw drop, no ballad piano, no male voices, no sampled voice hooks.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - synth brass stab and nylon guitar flourish]

[Verse 1 - lead soprano]
Strawberry yoghurt, top shelf, at the front
My name on the lid in black Sharpie
Seven in the morning, I open the fridge
And there's nothing on the shelf but a spoon

[Pre-Chorus - low alto]
Somebody in this flat
Has got some explaining to do

[Chorus - group chant]
Name on the lid! (Name on the lid!)
Who ate it? Who ate it?
Name on the lid! (Name on the lid!)
I wrote it big and I underlined it

[Verse 2 - spoken rap]
Jess is vegan, okay, that's a solid alibi
Priya slept at her boyfriend's, she's got the bus ticket
Leah's very quiet, Leah's very quiet
Leah, why is there pink on your chin?

[Chorus - group chant]
Name on the lid! (Name on the lid!)
Leah ate it! Leah ate it!
Name on the lid! (Name on the lid!)
She says she thought Maya was the brand

[Bridge - belted high note]
It's my name, Leah, it's my name
I've lived here for two years

[Dance Break - half-time beat switch, synth brass and claps]

[Chorus - group chant, key change up]
Name on the lid! (Name on the lid!)
Leah, that's mine! Leah, that's mine!
Name on the lid! (Name on the lid!)
Next time I'm writing it on the spoon

[Outro - nylon guitar and claps]
New rule on the fridge door
Leah buys the four-pack every Friday

tracks.caption: Hard techno in the current festival style. tracks.title: Bijou
tracks.mood: sardonic, tight-jawed fury
tracks.subject: a rental viewing in Rathmines with forty other people where the agent calls a cupboard the second bedroom
tracks.caption: Irish post-punk in the current Dublin style. A melodic bass guitar picked high on the neck carrying the main riff; an angular clean guitar soaked in chorus playing clipped stabs, switching to blown-out fuzz in the choruses; tight motorik drums with a dry snare and loud floor toms; a droning organ note under the last chorus. Dry and close with little reverb, the bass and drums forward, the guitars lower in the mix. Male voice, a flat Dublin baritone in deadpan half-spoken Sprechgesang, chanting the chorus rather than belting it. 146 BPM, E minor. Sardonic, tight-jawed fury. No jangly indie-pop guitars, no big singalong chorus, no britpop swagger, no autotune, no synth pads, no American pop-punk.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - high melodic bass riff and dry drums]

[Verse 1]
Saturday viewing, Rathmines, half ten
Forty of us on the stairs, a queue out past the Spar
Agent in a gilet with a clipboard and a grin
Says have your references ready, it's very competitive

[Chorus]
Bijou, he says, bijou
The second bedroom is a press with a door
Bijou, he says, bijou
Two thousand one hundred a month

[Verse 2]
The shower's in the kitchen, he calls it open plan
There's a futon on the boiler, he calls it flexible
A lad behind me's offering six months up front
A girl is crying quietly in the hot press

[Chorus]
Bijou, he says, bijou
The second bedroom is a press with a door
Bijou, I say, bijou
And I hand him my references anyway

[Bridge - fuzz guitar and floor toms]
Bank statements, payslips, a letter from my mam
A letter from my mam to say I'm very tidy

[Outro - bass alone, then cut]
He'll be in touch
He won't be in touch

[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.title: Padel Court
tracks.mood: furious, proud, ready for the pit
tracks.subject: the council turning the town's only skatepark into padel courts
tracks.caption: Groove hardcore punk in the genre-blending 2025 style. Chunky palm-muted downtuned guitars playing groove riffs that drop into two-step and half-time breakdowns; a groove-heavy live drum kit with loud floor toms, bursts of d-beat and choked crash cymbals; congas and hand percussion under a dreamy clean-guitar interlude; a warm synth pad swelling under the sung bridge. Raw and roomy, the guitars and drums forward, the bass thick under the riffs. Male voice, a hoarse shouted lead answered by a gang of shouting voices on the hook, switching to a soft reverbed sung voice for the bridge. 168 BPM with half-time breakdowns, D minor. Furious, proud, ready for the pit. No polished pop-punk chorus, no metalcore growls, no thrash-metal shredding or guitar solos, no autotune, no trap drums, no EDM drop.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - palm-muted downtuned riff and floor toms, short]

[Verse 1]
Twelve years we rode the bowl behind the leisure centre
I broke my wrist on that coping when I was fourteen
Council sent a letter on Monday, exciting news
Now there's chain-link round it and a man with a digger

[Chorus - gang shouts answer]
Padel court! (No!)
Forty quid an hour! (No!)
Where are the kids meant to go?
Padel court! (No!)

[Verse 2]
Glass walls and a booking app
Four dentists in white visors playing doubles
We sat on the kerb with our boards across our knees
Watching them miss the ball

[Breakdown - half-time, gang shouts]
Booking fee! Booking fee!
Ten-minute grace period!

[Chorus - gang shouts answer]
Padel court! (No!)
Forty quid an hour! (No!)
They can keep their little rackets
Padel court! (No!)

[Bridge - clean guitar, congas and a soft synth pad, sung quietly]
Top floor of the multi-storey after six
Nobody parks up there and the concrete's smooth

[Outro - full band, last breakdown, gang shout]
See you on the top floor
Bring a broom!

[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.title: Wrong Way On Purpose
tracks.mood: cheeky, grown and sweet on her
tracks.subject: a husband who turns left when the whole Friday line dance at the Elks Lodge turns right, so that for one count of eight he is facing his wife of thirty years
tracks.caption: Modern Southern soul in the drum-machine line-dance style of the Black Southern club circuit. A programmed drum-machine shuffle with stacked handclaps on two and four; a warm synth bass walking the two-step groove; keyboard horn stabs and short organ chords answering each line; a bluesy electric lead guitar filling the gaps with bent notes. Warm, close and plain, the drums and voice forward, the keys in the middle. Male voice, a gritty conversational baritone, a grown storyteller who talks the dance-step cues and sings the hook while a crowd answers him. 96 BPM, B-flat major. Cheeky, grown and sweet on her. No vintage live horn section or 1960s Stax-style live band, no gospel choir, no country twang, no zydeco accordion, no trap drums, no autotune.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - drum-machine shuffle, handclaps and an organ stab]

[Verse 1]
Friday night at the Elks Lodge, DJ Ray calls the slide
Forty of us in four straight lines on the hardwood floor
Thirty years my baby's been dancing on my left
Brings her good shoes in a grocery bag and dances in her flats

[Pre-Chorus]
Quarter-turn, the whole room swings to the right
And I go left

[Chorus]
Wrong way on purpose (On purpose!)
Whole room's looking at the wall and I'm looking at you
Eight counts face to face, then I fall back in line
Wrong way on purpose (On purpose!)

[Verse 2]
Little man at the front says Mister, you messing up the line
His grandmama says hush, he been doing that since ninety-six
My wife rolls her eyes like she ain't been waiting all week
Then she winks at me on the count of eight

[Spoken - dance cues]
Now slide to the right, now bring it on back
Everybody turn... well, almost everybody

[Chorus]
Wrong way on purpose (On purpose!)
Whole room's looking at the wall and I'm looking at you
Thirty years and I still ain't learned it right
Wrong way on purpose (On purpose!)

[Outro - organ, handclaps and a guitar fill]
Last song, that little man turns left too
And his grandmama hollers Lord, it's catching

tracks.title: Still Blue On Tuesday
tracks.mood: wild, giddy and still covered in paint
tracks.subject: turning up to the office on Tuesday still blue from J'ouvert paint after Labor Day in Brooklyn
tracks.caption: Power soca in the Brooklyn Labor Day carnival style. A driving four-on-the-floor kick with syncopated snare and tom fills; iron brake-drum percussion ringing on steady eighths; a steelpan playing the main riff over a punchy brass-section line; a bright sawtooth synth lead doubling the brass on the drop; a crowd breakdown where everything stops except the iron. Loud, bright and wide, the kick and iron forward, the brass high in the mix. Male voice, a Trinidadian-English road-march chanter, shouting commands and singing the hook while a crowd answers every line. 156 BPM, G major. Wild, giddy and still covered in paint. No reggaeton dembow, no afrobeats guitar, no dancehall one-drop, no trap hi-hats, no autotune.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - iron and steelpan riff, kick enters]

[Verse 1]
Monday morning, six o'clock on Flatbush Avenue
J'ouvert, somebody throw a bucket of blue
In my ears, in my teeth, in my good white sneakers
I was jumping on the road till the sun come through

[Pre-Chorus]
Wave! (Wave!)
Jump! (Jump!)

[Chorus]
Still blue on Tuesday (Blue!)
Boss in the meeting looking at my ears (Blue!)
Scrubbed it three times and it won't come off
Still blue on Tuesday

[Verse 2]
Rode the 2 train blue and everybody knew
Lady from Grenada say you play mas, you?
Laptop open on the spreadsheet, I'm a professional
Blue fingerprints on every key

[Pre-Chorus]
Wave! (Wave!)
Wine! (Wine!)

[Chorus]
Still blue on Tuesday (Blue!)
HR send a email, subject paint (Blue!)
Scrubbed it four times and it won't come off
Still blue on Wednesday

[Breakdown - everything stops except the iron]
Everybody who still blue, put your hand up!
(Hand up!)

[Outro - full band, then iron alone]
Still blue, still blue
Next year I'm going green

tracks.title: Pocket Dial
tracks.mood: tender and blurred, holding on to something ordinary
tracks.subject: a four-minute pocket-dial voicemail of your father washing up and whistling
tracks.caption: Shoegaze revival in the current nu-gaze style. Walls of fuzz guitar through a heavy fuzz pedal, with glide-guitar whammy bends and reverse-reverb swells, drop-tuned so the low chords feel heavy; a bass guitar doubling the root notes underneath; drums washed in constant ride and crash with the snare half-buried; a single quiet clean guitar playing alone in the intro. Loud, blurred and wide, the guitars dominant, the voice sitting just inside the guitars and slightly clearer in the verses. Female voice, breathy and airy in a soft high register, sitting just inside the guitars with every word still audible. 84 BPM, D major. Tender and blurred, holding on to something ordinary. No clean pop vocal on top, no trap drums, no autotune, no metal growls, no acoustic folk strumming, no pedal steel or slowcore.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - one clean guitar, then a fuzz swell, short]

[Verse 1]
Tuesday, six-fourteen, a missed call from Dad
Four minutes twelve seconds and nobody talking
Just the tap running and the radio on low
And him whistling the same three notes

[Chorus]
Pocket dial, pocket dial
You don't know I'm listening
Plates in the rack and the kettle starting
Pocket dial

[Verse 2]
I can hear the dog's tags on her bowl
I can hear you tell her not yet
You say right then to nobody at all
You've said that every evening I can remember

[Chorus]
Pocket dial, pocket dial
You don't know I'm listening
I won't call back, you'd only say hello
Pocket dial

[Instrumental Break - fuzz guitar wall with glide bends]

[Bridge - guitars swell and blur]
I saved it to the cloud, I saved it twice
Four minutes twelve seconds of you washing up

[Outro - fuzz falls away, clean guitar alone]
I play it on the train when it's dark out
It ends when you sit down on the phone

tracks.title: Di Bawah Helm
tracks.mood: tired and quietly grateful, swelling into a full room singing back
tracks.subject: an ojek driver who works Sundays and listens to the sermon on one earbud in the church car park between rides, singing the closing worship song under his helmet while he waits for the next order
tracks.caption: Indonesian praise and worship in the live megachurch ballad style. Wide analog-style synth pads swelling under every section; an ambient electric guitar with dotted-eighth delay and shimmer reverb playing volume-swelled single notes; a Rhodes electric piano holding the chords; electric bass on steady root eighths; drums that start on soft floor-tom pulses, move to a soft straight backbeat with closed hi-hats in the verses and open into a four-on-the-floor kick with crash washes for the bridge build. A wide, roomy live-church sound, the pads and the lead vocal forward, a congregation singing the chorus and bridge back from behind. Male worship leader, warm clean baritone that opens into a strong belt on the chorus, plain conversational Indonesian phrasing. 72 BPM, A major. Tired and quietly grateful, swelling into a full room singing back. No EDM drop, no trap hi-hats, no autotune, no rap, no gospel choir runs.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - synth pad swell and one delayed guitar note]

[Verse 1]
Minggu pagi aku antar ibu ke gereja
Dia masuk, aku parkir di bawah ketapang
Jaket hijau, helm belum kulepas
Kiri buat khotbah, kanan buat orderan

[Pre-Chorus]
Pendeta bilang, "Yang letih, datanglah"
Aku kira itu buat yang di dalam aja

[Chorus]
Tuhan, aku di parkiran
Helm di kepala, mesin belum dingin
Mereka nyanyi di dalam gedung
Aku ikut pelan di bawah helm ini

[Verse 2]
Lagu penutup mulai dari dalam
Tukang parkir ikut nyanyi, peluitnya di saku
Earphone kananku bunyi, orderan masuk
Aku biarin lewat, satu lagu lagi aja

[Chorus]
Tuhan, aku di parkiran
Helm di kepala, mesin belum dingin
Orderan lewat, nggak apa-apa
Lagu ini buat yang di luar juga

[Bridge - floor toms turn into four-on-the-floor, the congregation sings each line back]
Dari gedung sampai parkiran
(Dari gedung sampai parkiran)
Engkau dengar semuanya
(Engkau dengar semuanya)

[Chorus - full band, the whole room sings]
Tuhan, aku di parkiran
Helm di kepala, mesin belum dingin
Ibu tadi keluar, naik motorku lagi
Kami nyanyi berdua sampai rumah

[Outro - pad alone, one delayed guitar note fading]

tracks.title: Tiga Ratus Petir
tracks.mood: giddy and breathless, a festival-night rush
tracks.subject: the girl at a festival's glitter face-paint booth who paints the same lightning bolt on three hundred faces before the headliner, then paints one on herself and runs for the main stage
tracks.caption: Indonesian festival EDM in the future-bass style, with a traditional string hook. A plucked Sumba jungga, a bright two-string lute, playing a short pentatonic riff over sustained pads in the intro and returning between vocal lines; stacked supersaw chords sidechained hard to the kick; LFO-wobbled future-bass chords in the drops, felt in half-time; a deep 808 sub under the drops; snare rolls and white-noise risers into each drop, with fast hi-hat rolls only in the breakdown. Glossy and wide, the jungga and the lead vocal forward in the verses, the chords huge and pumping in the drops. Bright, clear female pop voice, light and conversational in the verses and belting the hook, mixing Indonesian lines with short English phrases, one live singer throughout. 144 BPM, F major. Giddy and breathless, a festival-night rush. No sampled voice hooks, no formant-shifted ad-libs, no dubstep growl bass, no trap beat under the verses, no big-room house drop, no autotune, no rap verse.

[Intro - plucked jungga riff over a soft pad]

[Verse 1]
Jam tiga sore aku buka meja lipat
Glitter emas, kuas kecil, cermin retak

Jam delapan tanganku udah hafal

Cowok berkumis minta petir di jidat

Kuasku gemetar, glitternya tinggal dikit

[Chorus]
One more bolt, satu lagi

tracks.title: Gerbang Jam Sepuluh
tracks.mood: bratty, gleeful and built to be shouted back
tracks.subject: climbing the locked boarding-house gate at eleven at night after a gig while the landlady waits on the porch with a flashlight
tracks.caption: Indonesian pop punk in the 2000s Jakarta sing-along style. Two distorted electric guitars playing palm-muted downstroked power chords in the verses and opening into octave-riff leads on the chorus; a bright keytar synth line doubling the chorus melody; picked electric bass locked to root eighths; drums playing a driving eighth-note backbeat in the verses and flipping to a fast skate-punk beat with the snare on every upbeat in the choruses, crash-ride accents and a half-time breakdown before the last chorus. Loud, tight and bright, the guitars wide left and right, the lead vocal forward and dry, the gang shouts right behind it. Bright, slightly nasal young male lead, cheeky and fast, with a gang of friends shouting 'whoa-oh' and the answer lines. 184 BPM, E major. Bratty, gleeful and built to be shouted back. No screaming, no metalcore breakdown, no emo minor-key drama, no autotune, no trap drums.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - palm-muted guitars, four clicks on the hi-hat]

[Verse 1]
Manggung di kafe, dibayar nasi kotak
Encore dua kali, gue lupa lihat jam
Ojek nurunin gue di mulut gang
Gerbang kos udah digembok dari dalam

[Pre-Chorus]
Pesan Ibu Kos di grup jelas banget
"Lewat jam sepuluh, tidur di luar!"

[Chorus - gang shouts]
Whoa-oh, gerbang jam sepuluh
Gitar di punggung, sandal di tangan
Whoa-oh, gue manjat pelan-pelan
Asal Ibu Kos udah tidur, aman

[Verse 2]
Kaki kanan di gembok, kaki kiri di pot
Celana nyangkut di ujung besi pagar
Sret! Robek dari lutut sampai saku
Terus ada senter nyala di teras

[Bridge - half-time breakdown, the gang answers each line]
"Jam berapa ini?" (Jam sebelas, Bu!)
"Kamu kira ini hotel?" (Bukan, Bu!)
"Turun dari situ!" (Iya, Bu!)
"Uang kos bulan ini?" (Besok, Bu!)

[Chorus - double-time, gang shouts]
Whoa-oh, gerbang jam sepuluh
Gitar di punggung, celana robek
Whoa-oh, Ibu Kos buka gembok
"Ibu nonton live-mu. Besok pulang jam sepuluh!"

[Outro - one last power chord ringing out]
Whoa-oh, besok jam sepuluh

tracks.title: Bentar Lagi Jalan
tracks.mood: exasperated and bouncing, laughing through the wait
tracks.subject: a new employee stuck in an empty angkot at the terminal while the driver waits for it to fill up and keeps saying it is leaving any minute
tracks.caption: Indonesian ska punk in the 90s Jakarta style. Offbeat electric guitar skanks, muted upstroke chops on every 'and'; a combo organ bubbling on the offbeats; a horn section of trumpet, trombone and tenor sax playing short unison riffs that answer each vocal line; a bouncy electric bass walking between chord tones; drums playing a fast ska beat with eighth-note hi-hats and the snare on two and four, switching into punk double-time for the choruses. Bright and live, the horns and the lead vocal forward, the drums roomy. Shouted-sung male lead, playful and a little hoarse, with a crowd of male voices chanting the answer lines. 172 BPM, B-flat major. Exasperated and bouncing, laughing through the wait. No reggae one-drop, no slow dub bass, no pop-rock ballad chorus, no autotune, no synth leads.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - horn riff over the guitar skank]

[Verse 1]
Hari pertama kerja, aku naik angkot biru
Jam tujuh kurang, cuma aku sama sopir
Mesin nyala, radio muter dangdut
Tapi rodanya nggak gerak dari tadi

[Pre-Chorus]
Aku tanya, "Bang, kapan berangkat?"
Dia ngelap kaca, terus jawab santai

[Chorus - the crowd chants the answers]
"Bentar lagi jalan!" (Bentar lagi!)
Udah setengah jam, belum jalan
"Bentar lagi jalan!" (Bentar lagi!)
Aku masuk kantor jam delapan, Bang!

[Verse 2]
Naik ibu-ibu bawa dua karung bawang
Naik anak SMA, naik bapak bawa ayam
Bangku udah penuh, ayamnya di pangkuanku
Sopirnya masih teriak, "Masih muat, masih muat!"

[Bridge - horns go double-time, the crowd answers]
"Geser dikit, Neng!" (Udah mentok, Bang!)
"Geser dikit, Pak!" (Ayamnya protes!)

[Chorus - the crowd chants the answers]
"Bentar lagi jalan!" (Akhirnya jalan!)
Dua ratus meter, "Kiri, Bang!"
Kantor baruku ternyata dekat banget
Besok aku jalan... kaki aja!

[Outro - horns and the crowd chant, then a hard stop]
Bentar lagi jalan... kaki!

[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.title: Pinjol
tracks.genre: classic dangdut, Soneta-style orkes Melayu rock
tracks.mood: a comic cautionary tale, scolding with a wink
tracks.subject: a man who took an online loan to buy a new phone, and the debt collector messages everyone in his contacts, starting with his mother-in-law
tracks.caption: Classic Indonesian dangdut in the 1970s Soneta orkes Melayu rock style. Paired gendang hand drums playing the classic dang-dut groove, a high slap leading into a low open boom at the end of each bar; a bamboo suling flute filling the gaps between vocal lines; a mandolin playing tremolo melodies in the intro and between verses; an overdriven hard-rock electric guitar playing riffs and one short solo; a Hammond-style organ with a simple bass and kit backbeat underneath. A warm, slightly roomy live 70s orkes sound, the gendang, mandolin and lead vocal forward, the guitar loud in the breaks. Male lead with Malay cengkok ornaments and long melismatic held notes at phrase ends, and a female voice singing the quoted lines in the second verse. 124 BPM, A minor. A comic cautionary tale, scolding with a wink. No fast koplo kendang, no EDM beat, no autotune, no trap drums, no modern pop production.

tracks.mood: comic and swaying, a sly village tall tale
tracks.subject: three men on the village ronda night-watch post who are meant to patrol and spend the night arguing over a game of gaple, while a chicken thief walks past behind them
tracks.caption: Campursari, the Central Javanese gamelan-and-keyboard style of the Didi Kempot era. Saron and demung playing the balungan melody, with kempul and a large gong marking the end of each phrase; a plucked siter zither rippling between vocal lines; kendhang ciblon driving a swaying dance groove; keroncong cak and cuk ukuleles strumming on the offbeats; soft keyboard string pads, a bass guitar and suling flute fills. Warm and roomy, the gamelan and the lead voice forward, the keyboard strings soft behind them. Warm male crooner singing in plain Indonesian with Javanese cengkok ornaments and a sly storytelling grin in the voice, a female sinden voice echoing short Javanese phrases in the chorus. 88 BPM, E minor. Comic and swaying, a sly village tall tale. No dangdut koplo beat, no rock drums, no EDM, no autotune, no rap.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - siter ripple, saron melody, one gong]

[Verse 1]
Malam Jumat, jadwal ronda kami bertiga
Pak Darno, Mas Joko, sama aku
Senter, sarung, kentongan di tiang
"Keliling nanti, habis satu putaran"

[Pre-Chorus]
Satu putaran jadi sebelas
Kuping Mas Joko penuh jepitan jemuran

[Chorus - the sinden echoes]
Gaple, gaple di pos ronda
Kartu dibanting, plak! sampai pagi
Kampung aman, katanya (jarene...)
Mata kami cuma ke meja

[Verse 2]
Di belakang lewat orang pakai sarung
Jalan pelan, pikul karung goni
Dari karungnya ada bunyi "petok"
Pak Darno bilang, "Sst! Aku lagi mikir"

[Chorus - the sinden echoes]
Gaple, gaple di pos ronda
Kartu dibanting, plak! sampai pagi
Ada yang lewat di belakang (liwat, liwat...)
Kami masih ribut soal balak enam

[Bridge - kendhang ciblon drops to a hush, then picks up]
Subuh-subuh Pak RT lari pakai singlet
"Jagoku hilang! Yang ronda ke mana?"
Kami bertiga angkat tangan, jepitan masih di kuping

[Chorus - the sinden echoes]
Gaple, gaple di pos ronda
Kartu dibanting, plak! sampai pagi
Kampung aman, katanya (jarene...)
Jago Pak RT udah sampai kampung sebelah

[Outro - siter and gong, the voice nearly alone]
Minggu depan kartunya disita (wis, wis...)

tracks.title: Antre Bimbingan
tracks.mood: bright, shy and hopeful
tracks.subject: falling for the girl who waits in the same thesis-supervision queue outside a lecturer's office every Tuesday
tracks.caption: Indonesian guitar pop in the 2000s Jogja band style. Chiming clean electric guitars on the edge of breakup playing arpeggiated open chords; an acoustic guitar doubling the strum; a melodic electric bass moving between chord tones; drums playing a straight-eighth rock beat with open hi-hat and a tambourine on two and four; a few piano chords under the last chorus. Clean, bright and band-in-a-room, the guitars forward and wide, the voice in the middle, no heavy distortion. Warm, slightly nasal light-baritone male voice, plain and conversational, with an 'oh-oh' singalong hook the band sings along to. 128 BPM, G major. Bright, shy and hopeful. No synths, no power-ballad build, no Malay melisma, no autotune, no electronic drums.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - jangling guitar arpeggio, then the band]

[Verse 1]
Selasa pagi di lantai tiga
Kursi plastik depan ruangan Bu Ratna
Kamu bab dua, aku bab empat
Kertas kita sama-sama penuh coretan merah

[Pre-Chorus]
Kamu pinjam stabilo, aku pinjam stapler
Kita sama-sama pura-pura nggak gugup

[Chorus - the band sings the oh-oh]
Oh-oh, antre bimbingan
Kamu nomor tujuh, aku delapan
Bu Ratna, tolong datang telat lagi
Aku belum berani minta nomormu

[Verse 2]
Minggu ketiga aku bawa dua gorengan
Satu buat aku, satu "kebetulan lebih"
Kamu bilang revisimu disuruh ulang
Aku bilang punyaku juga, padahal nggak

[Chorus - the band sings the oh-oh]
Oh-oh, antre bimbingan
Kamu nomor tujuh, aku delapan
Bu Ratna, lama banget di dalam
Gorengan kita udah dingin

[Bridge - guitars drop to one arpeggio, tambourine keeps time]
Kalau nanti kita sama-sama lulus
Selasa pagi aku ke mana?
Aku tulis nomorku pelan-pelan
Di pojok kertas revisimu

[Chorus - full band, everyone on the oh-oh]
Oh-oh, antre bimbingan
Kamu nomor tujuh, aku delapan
Kamu masuk duluan, kamu senyum
Kertasnya kamu bawa, nomorku juga

[Outro - guitar arpeggio rings out, one last tambourine hit]

tracks.title: Katanya
tracks.mood: wry and scolding, a sisterly telling-off
tracks.subject: the neighbourhood WhatsApp group forwarding a warning about a kidnapper disguised as a balloon seller, and the whole street chasing Pak Udin, who has sold balloons there for twenty years
tracks.caption: Qasidah modern in the Semarang orkes style of the 1980s, the Nasida Ria lineage. Rebana and terbang frame drums in interlocking patterns over a light, steady kit backbeat with tambourine; a violin playing the main melody with Middle Eastern-flavoured runs; a suling flute answering between lines; a combo organ holding the chords; clean electric guitar and bass in a simple orkes groove. Lightly produced and a little roomy, the voices and rebana forward, the violin bright on top. An all-female vocal group singing in unison and two-part harmony, alternating with one clear female solo lead who tells the story in plain Indonesian. 112 BPM, D minor. Wry and scolding, a sisterly telling-off. No solo devotional pop, no Arabic chanting, no dangdut gendang groove, no mandolin, no male lead, no EDM, no rock guitar solo, no autotune.

tracks.title: Panjat Pinang
tracks.mood: cheeky, flirty and slapstick
tracks.subject: a young man climbing the greased pole at the Independence Day contest to win the bicycle prize for the girl across the alley, sliding down every time while she heckles him in pantun
tracks.caption: Gambang kromong in the Betawi kombinasi style, the Jakarta Chinese-Peranakan ensemble with a modern rhythm section. A gambang wooden xylophone and a row of kromong kettle gongs carrying the melody together; tehyan and kongahyan bowed fiddles playing the same line in nasal heterophony; a bamboo suling and kecrek metal clappers on the accents; kendang driving a bouncing street-party groove, with an electric bass and a light drum kit underneath. Bright, busy and street-party loud, the fiddles and the two voices forward, the gongs ringing behind. A nasal male singer and a sharp-tongued female singer trading Betawi pantun in call-and-response, comic and quick, a street crowd answering in the chorus. 118 BPM, F major. Cheeky, flirty and slapstick. No keroncong strumming, no dangdut koplo beat, no pop ballad, no autotune, no EDM.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - gambang and tehyan melody, kendang kicks in]

[Verse 1 - male singer, pantun]
Kerak telor dimasak di atas arang
Kelapanya disangrai sampe wangi
Abang manjat pinang buat Neng seorang
Sepeda merah di pucuk, buat Neng nanti

[Verse 2 - female singer answers in pantun]
Ondel-ondel diarak keliling taman
Mukanya merah, matanya melotot
Abang ngomongnya kayak jagoan
Baru sejengkal udah melorot

[Chorus - duet, the crowd answers]
Panjat pinang, Bang, panjat pinang
Pinangnya licin, omongan Abang lebih licin
Sekali lagi! (Sekali lagi!)
Jatoh lagi! (Ya ampun, Bang!)

[Verse 3 - male and female trading lines]
Celana kolor udah item kena oli
"Muka Abang juga item, mane muka, mane kolor?"
Aye injek pundak Si Mamat, tinggal sejengkal
"Awas, Bang, Si Mamat udah gemeteran!"

[Chorus - duet, the crowd answers]
Panjat pinang, Bang, panjat pinang
Pinangnya licin, omongan Abang lebih licin
Sekali lagi! (Sekali lagi!)
Dapet, Bang! (Dapet sepedanya!)

[Bridge - kendang break, the fiddles hold one note]
"Sepedanya diturunin... eh, roda tiga!"
Ini mah buat bocah, Neng, maapin Abang
"Kagak ape, Bang, nyang penting Abang manjat
Besok Abang nyang naik, aye nyang dorong"

[Outro - gambang and fiddles, a last gong]
Abang nyang naik, aye nyang dorong

tracks.title: Lampu Cumi
tracks.mood: proud, salty and rowdy
tracks.subject: a squid-fishing crew stringing green lamps on their boat and racing the other boats out of Indramayu harbour at dusk
tracks.caption: Indonesian surf rock in the 1960s instrumental-band tradition, played by a modern West Java coast band. A clean lead electric guitar drenched in a spring-reverb tank playing rapid double-picked tremolo melodies with whammy-bar dips and reverb drips; a second guitar strumming reverb-soaked rhythm chords; a round electric bass driving the root notes; drums playing a pounding floor-tom surf beat with tom rumbles and the snare on two and four. Live and tight but wet with spring reverb, the lead guitar forward, the vocal rough and close. Rough, gritty male lead voice singing clear, plain melodies, with the boat crew shouting only the one-word answers. 168 BPM, E minor. Proud, salty and rowdy, a crew heading out to sea at dusk. No pop-punk chorus, no swing rhythm, no distorted metal guitar, no synths, no autotune.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - short spring-reverb tremolo pickup over floor toms, four bars]

[Verse 1]
Jam lima sore di muara Indramayu
Tiga puluh lampu kami ikat di tiang
Solar penuh, es balok dua ton
Mesin batuk dua kali, terus jalan

[Chorus - the crew shouts the answers]
Lampu cumi! (Nyalakan!)
Hijau di tengah laut gelap
Lampu cumi! (Nyalakan!)
Cumi naik ke lampu kami

[Verse 2]
Kapal Haji Darman nyalip dari kiri
Juragan teriak, "Gas! Jangan kalah!"
Ombak setinggi pintu, kopi tumpah di dek
Kami yang duluan sampai di karang

[Instrumental Break - tremolo lead guitar with whammy dips]

[Chorus - the crew shouts the answers]
Lampu cumi! (Nyalakan!)
Hijau sampai kelihatan dari darat
Lampu cumi! (Nyalakan!)
Cumi naik ke lampu kami

[Bridge - bass and floor toms alone, then the guitars crash back in]
Tiga minggu lagi kami pulang
Bawa cumi kering seratus karung
Kalau malam kamu lihat laut, Nak
Lampu hijau paling ujung itu Bapak

[Outro - one last tremolo run and a spring-reverb crash]
Lampu cumi! (Nyalakan!)

[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.title: 大凶スタート
tracks.mood: bouncy, cheeky and self-affirming
tracks.subject: drawing daikyō, the worst possible fortune, at the shrine on New Year's morning and deciding it can only go up from here
tracks.caption: Japanese kawaii idol electro-pop, a small-unit girl-group dance single built on electronic production rather than a band sound. Plucked synth arpeggios in bright sixteenths; a bitcrushed square-wave lead riff answering each vocal line; a toy piano doubling the top melody in the chorus; a four-on-the-floor electro kick with a crisp clap on two and four; a sidechained synth bass pumping on the offbeats; a sparkle sound effect on each chorus entry. Glossy, bright and wide, built in eight-bar dance blocks, the voices forward and the arpeggios spread to the sides. Young female voices trading single lines in the verses with a cute, half-spoken delivery, the chorus sung by two or three voices doubled at the octave rather than a big group unison, with one short spoken aside at the end. 148 BPM, A major. Bouncy, cheeky and self-affirming. No synth brass, no glockenspiel, no stacked handclaps, no mass group chant, no rock guitars, no rap verse, no autotune, no dubstep drop, no ballad section.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - short plucked synth arpeggio and bitcrushed square-wave riff]

[Chorus]
大凶スタート 引いちゃった
ここから先は 上がるだけ

[Verse 1]
元日の朝 十時の神社
百円入れて 箱を振ったら
出てきた棒は 二十七番
巫女さんの手が 一瞬止まった

[Pre-Chorus]
「待ち人 来ず」「失せ物 出ず」
「学業 危うし」 え、ぜんぶ?

[Chorus]
大凶スタート 引いちゃった
ここから先は 上がるだけ
細く折って 枝に結ぶ
ねえ これって レアでしょ?

[Verse 2]
中吉と 吉の 友達が
「交換する?」って 笑うけど
写真に撮って 待ち受けにした
今年 いちばん 目立ってる

[Pre-Chorus]
甘酒 ひとくち 熱すぎた
これも 大凶の しわざかな

[Chorus]
大凶スタート 引いちゃった
ここから先は 上がるだけ
細く折って 枝に結ぶ
ねえ 私って レアでしょ?

[Outro - square-wave riff and sparkle, spoken]
来年は 凶くらいで いいかも

tracks.mood: patient, wry and quietly content on her own
tracks.subject: learning to cook rice in a clay donabe after the rice cooker dies, three burnt bottoms before one pot comes out right, eaten alone at the low table with a raw egg
tracks.caption: Japanese singer-songwriter acoustic ballad in the hiki-gatari guitar-and-voice style that grew on TikTok. A steel-string acoustic guitar strummed close to the mic, with beat two left empty in the verse pattern; a soft upright piano entering at the pre-chorus; a quiet string pad under the second chorus; a full drum kit coming in only for the last chorus, brushes first and then sticks. Dry and intimate, the voice upfront and close, the guitar centred, building from almost bare to a full band at the end. Young female voice, slightly breathy and conversational in the verses, opening into a clear belt in the last chorus, with no showy runs. 78 BPM, G major. Patient, wry and quietly content. No programmed drums, no trap beat, no autotune, no orchestra in the first half, no lo-fi tape hiss.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - steel-string acoustic guitar alone, beat two left empty]

[Verse 1]
十年使った 炊飯器が
日曜の朝 ランプが点かない
棚の奥から 出してきたのは
冬に一回 鍋をした 土鍋

[Pre-Chorus - piano enters]
三十分 お米を 水につけて
強火で ぐつぐつ 言うまで待つ

[Chorus]
まだ 蓋は開けない
弱火で 十三分
ぱちぱち鳴ったら 火を止めて
あと十分 まだ開けない

[Verse 2]
一回目は 底が真っ黒
二回目は スマホ見てて 焦がした
三回目は 火が強すぎた
重曹入れて 一晩つけた

[Pre-Chorus]
四回目は 土曜の夜七時
コンロの前から 一歩も動かない

[Chorus - full band, brushes then sticks, voice opens up]
もう 蓋を開けていい
弱火で 十三分
ぱちぱち鳴って 火を止めて
十分待った もういいよ

[Outro - acoustic guitar alone]
ちゃぶ台に 茶碗ひとつ
生卵割って しょうゆ少し
おこげは 最後にとっておく
炊飯器 もう買わなくていいか

tracks.title: あぶら少なめ
tracks.mood: flustered, determined, then quietly proud
tracks.subject: a ramen shop's new part-timer on her first Saturday lunch rush, learning the 36-button meal-ticket machine and the regulars' 'katame, koime, abura-sukuname' orders, and getting the last one right
tracks.caption: Japanese piano-trio band pop with no guitar at all, in the style of a drama-theme single. An acoustic piano playing the riff and the rhythmic comping in syncopated chords, a Rhodes taking over in the verses; a fingered electric bass doubling and answering the piano's left hand; live drums with tight sixteenth-note hi-hats and a ghost-noted snare; a light synth pad behind the chorus. Tight and clean with a live room feel, the piano and the voice forward, bass and kick locked in the centre. High male tenor, soulful but restrained with light melisma, flipping into falsetto on the chorus peaks. 118 BPM, Db major. Flustered, determined, then quietly proud. No electric guitar, no acoustic guitar, no EDM drop, no trap hi-hats, no autotune, no string orchestra.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - short piano riff with the bass doubling the left hand]

[Verse 1]
土曜の十一時 シャッターが上がる
もう列は 角の薬局まで
券売機には ボタンが三十六個
「味玉どこ?」って 聞かれても わからない

[Pre-Chorus]
カウンター越しに 食券を受け取って
「お好みは?」って 声が裏返る

[Chorus]
かため こいめ あぶら少なめ
早口すぎて 聞き取れない
メモの字が 湯気でにじむ
「すみません もう一回」

[Verse 2]
作業着の 常連さんに
あぶらだけ 普通で 出しちゃった
なんにも言わずに すすって
スープまで 飲んで 帰ってった

[Pre-Chorus]
一時五十八分 最後のひとり
食券置いて 小声で 早口

[Chorus]
かため こいめ あぶら少なめ
今度は 一回で 聞き取れた
メモの字が 湯気でにじむ
「かため こいめ すくなめ 入ります!」

[Bridge - piano and bass break, falsetto]
三十六個の ボタンより
三つの言葉が むずかしかった

[Outro - piano riff, band stops together]
のれんをしまって 店長が
「来週の土曜も 入れる?」

tracks.title: 火曜は燃える
tracks.mood: sly, funky and put-upon
tracks.subject: a newcomer's rubbish bag left behind with a yellow sticker, and the woman across the street who comes down to teach him the sorting rules
tracks.caption: Japanese funk-rock mixture band, live five-piece funk with rap-flow verses. Slap and fingered electric bass playing syncopated sixteenths; a choppy wah guitar and muted single-note funk guitar lines; clavinet comping with Rhodes and short organ swells; live drums in a hip-hop pocket with a dry snare, a laid-back kick and tight hi-hats; short clavinet-and-organ stabs at the ends of phrases. Dry and punchy, like a band playing together in one studio room, bass and voice forward, clav and guitar panned apart. Male lead half-rapping the verses in rhythmic Japanese wordplay and switching to a falsetto soul hook, with short ad-libs. 108 BPM, G minor. Sly, funky and put-upon. No programmed beat, no four-on-the-floor, no trap hi-hats, no autotune, no city-pop synth brass, no ballad section.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - slap bass riff, clavinet and dry snare]

[Verse 1]
引っ越し三日目 ポストに冊子
分別ガイドは 十二ページ
ラベル剥がして キャップは別
洗って 潰して 出すのは 第二木曜

[Pre-Chorus]
朝の集積所 向かいの二階
カーテンの隙間から 視線が刺さる

[Chorus]
火曜は燃える
燃えるゴミの日
黄色いシール 貼られて
俺の袋だけ 置いてかれた

[Verse 2]
傘は何ゴミ? フライパンは?
アプリに聞いても 「お問い合わせください」
向かいのおばちゃん 降りてきて
「あんた 新しい人?」って 袋を開けた

[Pre-Chorus]
十分間の 説教 最後にひとこと
「わかんなかったら うちに聞きな」

[Chorus]
火曜は燃える
燃えるゴミの日
今朝は シールなしで 持ってかれた
俺も ちょっと 燃えてきた

[Bridge - clavinet and slap bass break, ad-libs]
燃える 燃えない びん 缶 ペット
全部言えたら 手を叩け

[Outro - band stops dead on one hit]
来週は 粗大ゴミ
電話予約 何番だっけ
[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.title: 最後はカチャーシー
tracks.mood: rowdy, proud and joyful
tracks.subject: a Tokyo friend of the groom pulled up by the bride's grandmother to dance kachashi at the end of a three-hundred-guest Okinawan wedding reception
tracks.caption: Okinawan sanshin pop in the shima-uta band style, an up-tempo kachashi dance song. An Okinawan sanshin plucked with a horn plectrum, playing a bright melody on the Ryukyu scale; an acoustic guitar strumming underneath; a piano adding chords; a shimedaiko and paranku eisa-drum pattern driving the dance rhythm; finger whistles in the chorus. Warm, open and live, like a band on a wedding-hall stage, the sanshin and the voice forward, drums and whistles wide. Warm, plain male lead with a light Okinawan vowel colour, a crowd answering with the hayashi shouts written into the chorus. 138 BPM, C major. Rowdy, proud and joyful. No enka vibrato, no Amami falsetto flips, no reggae offbeat, no electronic drums, no autotune.

[Intro - short sanshin phrase on the Ryukyu scale over acoustic guitar]

新郎の挨拶 終わったはずが
三線が鳴って 全員立った

[Chorus]

ハイヤ 俺だけ 逆回り

足は 勝手に ついてきた

[Pre-Chorus]
指笛が 天井まで
新郎は もう 泣いている

[Chorus]
最後はカチャーシー
手のひら 上に 下に
イーヤーサーサー
おばぁより 先には 座れない

[Outro - eisa drums and finger whistles, sanshin plays the last phrase]
ハイヤ ハイヤ
東京に帰っても 手が回る

tracks.title: スヌーズ九回目
tracks.mood: frantic, silly and wide awake
tracks.subject: the ninth press of the snooze button and a ten-minute sprint for the 7:02 train
tracks.caption: J-core, Japanese rhythm-game hardcore techno. A distorted gabber kick on every beat with its tail tuned to the key; happy-hardcore piano stabs on the offbeats; a wide supersaw chord stack in the chorus; a squelching 303-style acid line in the verses; a breakdown of piano and supersaw with no kick, then a reverse-cymbal re-entry. Loud, bright and compressed, the kick and the voice forward, supersaws wide. High, bright young female voice, sung live and clearly in a cute anime register, short fast hook lines repeated. 190 BPM, F# minor. Frantic, silly and wide awake. No chopped voice samples, no sped-up nightcore voice, no dubstep wobble, no trap, no autotune, no slow ballad section.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - short supersaw stab and distorted kick roll]

[Verse 1]
六時ちょうどに 鳴ったはず
五分ごとに ボタン押して
気づけば 六時四十五分
これが 九回目の スヌーズ

[Pre-Chorus]
起きて 起きて 起きて 起きて
靴下 左右 ちがっても

[Chorus]
スヌーズ九回目 走れ 走れ
眉毛は 片方だけ 描いた
七時二分の 電車まで
あと十分 あと十分

[Breakdown - piano and supersaw, no kick]
ほんとは 一回目で 起きてた
目だけ 閉じて 聞いてた

[Verse 2]
トースト くわえて 鍵かけて
戻って ガスを 確かめて
階段 二段飛ばしで 下りて
定期は 部屋に 置いてきた

[Chorus]
スヌーズ九回目 走れ 走れ
改札 ピンポーン 残高不足
七時二分の 電車が行く
あと一本 あと一本

[Outro - kick drops out, alarm-like synth bleeps]
明日は 目覚まし 三個にする
[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.title: 最終のあとで
tracks.mood: proud, tireless and heroic
tracks.subject: the overnight track-maintenance crew who check and grind the rails between the last train at midnight and the first train at six
tracks.caption: Japanese melodic power metal, neoclassical speed metal. Neoclassical shred guitar with harmonic-minor sweep arpeggios and twin harmonised leads; a Hammond organ trading solos with the guitar; galloping palm-muted rhythm guitar; double-kick sixteenths under a snare on two and four; orchestral strings and a choir pad behind the chorus; a key change up a semitone into the last chorus. Big, wide and clean, the voice and the lead guitar forward, organ and strings filling the sides. Powerful high male tenor, clean and belted, with long sustained high notes and wide vibrato. 176 BPM, D minor. Proud, tireless and heroic. No harsh screams, no breakdowns, no rap, no idol vocals, no autotune, no nu-metal downtuning.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - short twin harmonised guitar lead over a double-kick gallop]

[Verse 1]
午前零時 最終が消えて
架線の電気が 落とされる
保線車両の ヘッドライトが
二本のレールを 白く照らす

[Pre-Chorus]
六時間で 四キロ先まで
五時半には 確認車が来る

[Chorus]
最終のあとで 俺たちが行く
誰も乗らない 線路を行く
ハンマーで ボルトを 叩いて
六時までに 線路を 返す

[Verse 2]
削正車の 火花が 散る
一ミリの 歪みを 削り取る
弁当は 三時に 立ったまま
ヘルメットの下で 湯気が上がる

[Pre-Chorus]
東の空が 少し 青い
最後のボルトに 白いしるし

[Instrumental Break - neoclassical guitar and Hammond organ duel]

[Chorus - key change up a semitone]
最終のあとで 俺たちが行く
誰も見てない 線路を行く
ハンマーで ボルトを 叩いて
始発に 線路を 返す

[Outro - strings and choir pad, one long held note]
線路脇で 始発を見送る
誰も 俺たちを 知らなくていい

tracks.mood: furious, petty and funny
tracks.subject: a man from Tokyo on his first Osaka trip explaining to an Osaka-born woman, at a takoyaki stall, how takoyaki is supposed to be eaten
tracks.caption: Kansai garage punk in the Kyoto riot-grrrl style, fast stop-start punk. Two overdriven electric guitars on cranked amps with almost no effects, playing choppy down-picked riffs with sudden dead stops; a picked electric bass locked to the kick; loose, fast live drums with abrupt tempo shifts and a half-time drop before the last chorus. Raw and roomy, recorded live in one room, guitars loud and voices forward, no polish. Female lead shouting and yelling in Kansai dialect, with deadpan spoken lines between shouts, and a female gang shouting the answer lines written in the lyrics. 196 BPM, E minor. Furious, petty and funny. No melodic singalong chorus, no guitar solo, no ska upstrokes, no pop-punk polish, no autotune.

tracks.title: 皿洗いは一本勝負
tracks.mood: flirty, amused and fond
tracks.subject: a couple settling whose turn it is to wash up with one round of an old two-player video game from his parents' house, where she has not lost in two years until she loses on purpose on his birthday
tracks.caption: Japanese chiptune swing pop, 8-bit pop. Two Famicom-style pulse-wave leads with a changing duty cycle; fast arpeggiated chip chords standing in for full chords; a triangle-wave bass walking in swing-jazz lines; noise-channel hi-hats and snare on swung eighths; short 8-bit fanfare turnarounds between sections. Clean and small, the chip voices close together with a little room, the voice forward and the pulse leads just behind it. Light, breathy female voice singing softly in a bossa-nova manner with no belt, playful and close. 136 BPM, F major. Flirty, amused and fond. No polysynth pads, no live drums, no EDM drop, no autotune, no rap, no straight eighths.

[Intro - short pulse-wave melody over a walking triangle bass, swung]

tracks.title: 二百十七番
tracks.mood: crushed, deadpan and bored out of its mind
tracks.subject: four hours on a ward office bench holding number ticket 217
tracks.caption: Japanese sludge and drone doom. Downtuned, fuzz-saturated guitar and bass through stacked amps, chords left to ring out into feedback; slow, heavy live drums with huge crash swells and long gaps between hits; a feedback drone section with no fixed meter; one sudden burst into a fast hardcore-punk tempo in the bridge before collapsing back to the crawl. Massive, loud and murky, guitars wall-to-wall, the voice distant and drenched in reverb. Male voice, low monotone chanting of short phrases, breaking into shouts in the fast burst. 60 BPM, C minor. Crushed, deadpan and bored out of its mind. No clean melodic chorus, no growled death-metal vocals, no shoegaze shimmer, no blast beats, no autotune.

tracks.title: 반납 1분 전
tracks.mood: a cool, quiet crush on a ride nobody wants to end
tracks.subject: riding Seoul public rental bikes along the Cheonggyecheon at midnight with someone met that evening, docking them one minute before the hour runs out
tracks.caption: Deep house idol pop in the current K-pop girl-group style, a club pulse rather than a ballad. A 909 kick on every beat with a soft clap on two and four; off-beat open hi-hats and a sixteenth-note shaker; a rolling, looping analog sub bassline that carries the groove and drops in and out between sections; a jazzy house piano playing 7th and 9th chords in short off-beat stabs; an M1-style organ stab answering each chorus line over a filtered pad. There is no drop: the energy rises and falls with low-pass filter sweeps and the bassline returning. Dry and close, the bassline and piano forward, hats spread wide, a short plate reverb on the voice only. Breathy mid-register female idol vocals in unison, restrained and conversational, almost spoken in the verses, singing one short English tag on the hook. 122 BPM, F minor. A cool, quiet crush on a ride nobody wants to end. No EDM drop, no trap hi-hats, no supersaw lead, no tropical-house plucks, no sampled voice hooks, no rap verse, no autotune, no ballad belting.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - 909 kick, rolling sub bassline and one house piano chord]

열한 시 오십 분, 청계천 입구
둘 다 따릉이 한 시간권 끊었지
너는 안장을 끝까지 올리고
나는 바구니에 네 가방을 실었어

[Chorus]
반납 일 분 전, 조금만 더 돌자
다리 하나만 더 지나가자
앱이 울려도 못 들은 척
One more minute, 천천히 밟아

[Verse 2]
광장시장 불은 벌써 꺼졌고

There is no drop: the energy rises and falls with low-pass filter sweeps and the bassline returning. A cool, quiet crush on a ride nobody wants to end. No EDM drop, no trap hi-hats, no supersaw lead, no tropical-house plucks, no sampled voice hooks, no rap verse, no autotune, no ballad belting.

tracks.title: 수건 치워
tracks.mood: petty, loud and ready to fight over a squat rack
tracks.subject: a towel left on the gym squat rack for forty minutes while its owner sits in the sauna
tracks.caption: Brazilian funk idol pop, the funk carioca beat inside a K-pop boy-group track. A programmed tamborzao drum pattern: a booming 808 kick with syncopated tom and conga hits in a three-three-two feel and a dry clap; a heavily saturated 808 sub bass that distorts on every hit; a stabby detuned square-synth riff of three notes looping through the whole song; a dry cowbell on the off-beats in the chorus. A sparse arrangement that adds one layer at a time and peaks in the last chorus. Dry, loud and narrow, the kick and sub forward, the lead voice centred and close. Male group vocals in punchy chanted talk-singing and rap, an MC-style lead with the whole group shouting the written answers on the hook. 130 BPM, G minor. Petty, loud and ready to fight over a squat rack. No trap hi-hat rolls, no Jersey club kicks, no reggaeton dembow, no live slap bass or horns, no sung ballad chorus, no autotune, no EDM drop.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - tamborzao drums and a three-note synth stab]

[Verse 1]
저녁 일곱 시, 하체 하는 날
스쿼트 랙 위에 하얀 수건 한 장

주인은 사우나에 들어간 지 사십 분

레그 익스텐션만 세 세트째

[Chorus]

자리 맡기 금지 (금지!)
랙 전세 냈어?
수건 치워 (치워! 치워!)

[Verse 2]
드디어 나온다, 얼굴이 빨개
머리에 수건 하나 더 두르고

형, 그건 쓰는 게 아니라 찜질이야

[Pre-Chorus]
카운터 누나도 보고 있어
안내문 붙은 지 벌써 한 달

수건 치워 (치워!)
자리 맡기 금지 (금지!)
땀은 사우나에서 다 뺐잖아
수건 치워 (치워! 치워!)

하나, 둘, 셋, 들어 올려
넷, 다섯, 여섯, 잘 봐 둬

[Outro - full beat, then a dead stop]
수건은 접어서 네 사물함에
랙은 이제 내 거야

[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.subject: a couple at Sinchon's summer water-gun festival who each sneak off to the same refill tap to ambush the other
tracks.caption: Afrobeats-groove idol pop, a summer K-pop girl-group track built on West African percussion. A shaker and conga loop with a rimshot clave pattern, a soft kick that skips beat three, and short talking-drum fills at the end of each section; a clean palm-muted highlife guitar playing interlocking arpeggios; a warm round sub bass holding long notes; marimba plucks doubling the hook melody; an airy synth pad held low under the chorus. Warm and roomy, the percussion spread wide, the guitar and the voice forward, light room reverb. A relaxed female lead in a sing-song melodic delivery with light melisma, with soft unison harmonies on a short chant-like hook. 104 BPM, D major. Giggly, sun-soaked and in love in the middle of a street water fight. No trap hi-hats, no EDM drop, no Rhodes R&B ballad feel, no reggaeton dembow, no amapiano log drums, no autotune.

tracks.title: 신랑 측 친구
tracks.mood: cool, sly flirting at a wedding desk
tracks.subject: staffing the bride's gift-money desk at a friend's wedding and flirting with the groom's friend at the next desk over a borrowed pen and the meal tickets
tracks.caption: Reggaeton idol pop in the current K-pop style. A programmed dembow riddim: a kick on every quarter note, snare and rimshot on the three-three-two syncopation, short reggaeton snare-roll fills into each chorus; a deep 808 sub bass following the kick; a plucked nylon-string guitar riff looping every four bars as the hook; sparse low piano chords; a white-noise riser into each chorus. Dry and tight, the kick, sub and guitar forward, the voices close with short delay throws on the line ends. A cool, laid-back female lead in half-rapped melodic flows, a relaxed male voice taking the second verse, and both together on the last chorus. 94 BPM, B minor. Cool, sly flirting at a wedding desk. No trap hi-hat rolls, no Brazilian funk tamborzao, no Afrobeats percussion, no acoustic bossa nova brushes, no EDM drop, no ballad belting, no autotune.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - nylon guitar riff over dembow drums]

[Verse 1 - Female Vocal]
신부 측 접수대, 오른쪽 끝자리
봉투 받고 이름 쓰고 식권 두 장
옆자리 신랑 측, 검은 넥타이
펜이 안 나온다며 내 걸 빌려 가

[Pre-Chorus]
식권은 몇 장 남았어?
나는 열둘, 너는?

[Chorus]
신랑 측 친구, 볼펜 돌려줘
그 펜 내 거잖아, 알면서
식 끝나면 같이 뷔페 가
줄 서는 동안 이름 알려 줘

[Verse 2 - Male Vocal]
신부 측 친구, 계산 또 틀렸지
만 원짜리 세다 두 번 웃었어
식장 문틈으로 축가 들을 때
내 쪽만 보는 거 다 봤어

[Pre-Chorus]
식권은 몇 장 남았어?
딱 두 장, 우리 거

[Chorus - Duet]
신랑 측 친구, 볼펜 돌려줘
"그냥 나 주면 안 돼?" 웃지 마
식 끝나면 같이 뷔페 가
갈비찜 앞에서 이름 알려 줘

[Outro - guitar riff alone, then one last kick]
부케는 못 받았어도
번호는 받았어

tracks.caption: Pop-punk boy-group rock, a polished major-key K-pop band track in a fast skate-punk feel. Double-tracked overdriven humbucker guitars play downstroked, palm-muted power chords in the verses and open ringing chords in the choruses, with an octave lead line as the hook; a picked electric bass follows the root in straight eighths; live drums play a fast two-beat with the snare on every upbeat in the verses, opening to crash-ride and a hard backbeat in the choruses; a thin synth layer sits under the guitars. Loud, bright and tight, guitars wide left and right, drums punchy, the lead vocal on top. A bright, youthful male unison lead, with the band shouting the written 'hey' answers on the hook. 176 BPM, B major. Furious at himself and laughing about it. No idol dance-pop beat, no raw street-punk sound, no metal screams, no EDM drop, no autotune.

tracks.title: 숨비소리
tracks.mood: proud, grand and windswept
tracks.subject: an eighty-one-year-old Jeju haenyeo's day in the water, from the dawn tide to the last whistle before she comes ashore
tracks.caption: Classical crossover male vocal quartet in the Korean popera style. A full orchestra: a string section in long legato lines, French horns carrying the main theme, timpani rolls under the climaxes and a harp playing rising arpeggios; a grand piano opening the song alone for four bars of slow broken chords; a rock rhythm section of live drums, bass and a sustained electric guitar entering only for the final chorus, which modulates up a whole step. Roomy and wide like a concert hall, the voices forward and the orchestra spread behind them, with a long natural hall reverb. Four male classical voices, bass, baritone, tenor and countertenor, with wide vibrato: solo verses passed from voice to voice, then all four in tutti harmony on the chorus, ending on a sustained high countertenor note. 72 BPM, E-flat major. Proud, grand and windswept. No pop drum loop, no electronic beat, no rap, no autotune, no musical-theatre dialogue.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - solo grand piano, four bars, harp joining on the last bar]

[Verse 1 - Baritone]
새벽 물때에 테왁을 메고
여든한 해의 바다로 가네
고무옷 소매 끝, 주름진 손등에
소금이 하얗게 말라 있네

[Verse 2 - Tenor]
한숨에 내려가 전복을 따고
한숨에 올라와 하늘을 보네
그 숨을 육십 년 세어 왔으니
바다가 평생의 집이었네

[Chorus - All four voices]
호오이, 숨비소리
물 위로 터지는 그 한 소리
오늘이 마지막 물질이라도
바다는 그 소리를 기억하리라

[Verse 3 - Bass]
갯바위에 모여 선 동생들이
물 위의 테왁을 보고 부르네
"삼촌, 오늘 망사리 무겁수다"
웃으며 할머니는 손을 흔드네

[Chorus - All four voices, up a whole step, full band enters]
호오이, 숨비소리
물 위로 터지는 오늘 마지막 소리
망사리 가득 어깨에 메고
할머니는 천천히 뭍으로 오네

[Outro - countertenor alone over harp, one held high note]
호오이

tracks.caption: Rockabilly in the Korean 'kimchibilly' style, a 1950s train-beat band. A slapped upright double bass with an audible click-slap on the backbeat, walking root and fifth; a hollowbody electric guitar with slapback echo and Bigsby vibrato twang, playing a fast lead riff and a short twangy solo; a small drum kit with a snare-heavy train beat, brushes in the verses and sticks in the choruses; a boogie-woogie piano pounding eighth-note fills. Dry and roomy like a small club stage, slapback echo on the guitar and the voice, the bass slap and the voice forward. A cocky male baritone croon with hiccups and short yelps, playful and fast. 168 BPM, A major. Frantic, cocky and grinning. No distorted punk guitars, no modern pop drums, no metal, no trot vibrato, no autotune.

[Verse 1]
주문 들어왔다, 짜장 둘에 탕수육
이화동 꼭대기, 계단 끝 파란 대문
철가방 꽉 묶고 헬멧 끈 당겨
면은 지금부터 오 분이면 불어

랩 씌운 짜장면, 불기 전에

할머니가 손 흔들어, "총각, 천천히!"

군만두는 서비스, 불기 전에

[Chorus]
불기 전에, 불기 전에
다음 집도 불기 전에

tracks.caption: Traditional Korean ska with a full horn section, upbeat and fast. An upstroke guitar skank on every off-beat; a Hammond organ doubling the off-beat skank in short percussive chops; a melodic electric bass walking under the verses; a four-piece horn section of trumpet, trombone, tenor sax and baritone sax playing unison riffs between the lines and a short trumpet solo; drums with rimshots on the backbeat, the hi-hat on the upbeats and a snare roll into each chorus. Roomy and live like a band on a club stage, horns wide, the voice and skank guitar forward. An easygoing male lead croon with a grin, and the band shouting the written group answers. 152 BPM, B-flat major. Rowdy, sweaty and far too competitive. No distorted punk guitars, no reggae one-drop slowdown, no pop drum machine, no rap, no autotune.

tracks.caption: Korean vocal jazz with an acoustic piano trio, a light medium swing. A walking upright bass in steady quarter notes; brushes on the snare with a swung ride cymbal and the hi-hat closing on two and four; an acoustic piano comping in rootless voicings with short answering fills after each line, and a sixteen-bar solo in the middle. Intimate and close like a small club, a dry room sound, the voice and piano forward, the bass warm and centred. A warm female voice with behind-the-beat phrasing, controlled vibrato on held notes and one short scat break. A short piano intro, then the trio swings. 126 BPM, F major. Tender and laughing. No programmed beats, no lo-fi hip-hop drums, no pop ballad strings, no horns, no R&B runs, no autotune.

아이스박스 테이프를 뜯으니

매직으로 꾹꾹 눌러 썼네

"그게 뭐였더라, 맛을 봐 봐"

짭짤하고 달고 조금 새콤해

tracks.caption: Blues power trio playing a heavy twelve-bar shuffle, guitar, bass and drums. An overdriven Stratocaster through a cranked tube amp, answering every vocal line with pentatonic string bends and taking a stinging solo; a bass guitar locked to the kick, walking the shuffle; drums playing a swung shuffle with ghost notes on the snare and a heavy backbeat. Live and loud in a small room, the guitar and voice forward, bass and kick tight together, short room reverb. A gritty, chesty male lead that leans hard on the last word of each line and leaves space for the guitar to answer. 116 BPM, E major. Angry, cold and grinning through gritted teeth. No fuzz-wall alternative rock, no metal riffing, no organ or horns, no pop chorus, no slow ballad, no autotune.

tracks.title: Sedondon
tracks.mood: sassy, smug and owning the room
tracks.subject: three office friends who turn up to the company annual dinner in the same emerald beaded baju kurung from the same Jalan TAR sale, and decide on the spot that it was the plan all along
tracks.caption: Malay idol pop in the K-pop-style girl-group performance format. A hard 808 sub-bass with fast trap hi-hat rolls under half-time verses; the chorus switching to a driving straight kick with hand claps on two and four; bold brass-section synth stabs punching the end of each sung line; a filtered white-noise riser into a short instrumental dance-break drop after the second chorus. Glossy and punchy, the kick and lead vocals forward, the brass stabs spread wide, short tight reverb. Three young female voices trading lines with confident, sassy delivery, the hook shouted in unison as a chant, one half-time rap verse, stacked harmonies only on the final chorus. 118 BPM, C# minor. Sassy, smug and owning the room. No reggaeton dembow, no swingbeat shuffle, no slow ballad section, no audible autotune, no EDM supersaw, no looping plucked-synth hook.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - 808 sub and brass synth stabs]

[Verse 1]
Annual dinner, hotel Shah Alam, tema "Malam Glamour"
Aku masuk dewan, baju kurung manik, hijau emerald
Toleh kiri, Ain pakai sama, manik sama, potongan sama
Toleh kanan, Mira pun sama. Alamak.

[Pre-Chorus]
Semua orang pandang
Kita pandang balik, okay?

[Chorus]
Sedondon, memang plan
(Plan! Plan!)
Tiga emerald, satu meja depan
Jangan tanya siapa tiru siapa
Malam ni dewan ni kita punya

[Verse 2 - Rap, half-time]
Boss tanya, "Tema group ke?" Kita angguk serentak
Kak HR snap gambar, terus naik story syarikat
Butik sama kat Jalan TAR, diskaun lima puluh peratus
Tiga orang kedekut, tiga orang paling bergaya

[Pre-Chorus]
Semua orang pandang
Kita senyum lagi, okay?

[Instrumental Break - filtered riser into a dance-break drop, brass stabs and claps]

[Chorus - three voices, stacked harmonies]
Sedondon, memang plan
(Plan! Plan!)
Tiga emerald naik pentas cabutan bertuah
Jangan tanya siapa tiru siapa
Sagu hati periuk nasi, kita kongsi

[Outro - brass stabs and one last clap]
Tahun depan, tema apa?
Sedondon.

tracks.title: Saga Merah
tracks.mood: earnest and happily in love, a refrain for a crowd to sing back
tracks.subject: a couple spending every Saturday for two years bringing a rusted 1989 Proton Saga back to life under her father's car porch, and the first drive to the beach with the windows wound down
tracks.caption: Malay arena pop-rock band anthem in the Insomniacks style. A clean electric guitar on the edge of breakup playing a dotted-eighth delay arpeggio in the intro and verses, opening into wide power chords in the chorus; piano doubling every chord change; a steady eighth-note bass pulse; a live drum kit with a floor-tom build and an open hi-hat and crash lift into each chorus. Polished radio production, roomy and wide, guitars and drums big but the lead vocal clearly on top. Earnest high male tenor, restrained and close in the verses and belted in the final chorus, with a gang of male voices singing the written 'oh-oh' line on the last chorus. 88 BPM, D major. Earnest and happily in love, a refrain made for a crowd to sing back. No fuzz or grunge distortion, no palm-muted punk drive, no orchestral strings, no slow rock kapak wailing guitar solo, no 6/8 power-ballad sway, no autotune, no EDM drop.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - delay guitar arpeggio and piano]

[Verse 1]
Saga merah, tahun lapan puluh sembilan
Tersadai bawah porch rumah ayah dia, empat-empat tayar kempis
Setiap Sabtu dia hulur spanar, aku baring bawah enjin
Tangan dia hitam minyak, dia kata, "Cantik, kan?"

[Pre-Chorus]
Dua tahun, tiga bateri
Satu karburetor kita cuci dalam sinki

[Chorus]
Pusing kunci, sekali lagi
Enjin batuk, enjin hidup
Dia jerit, satu taman dengar
Dan aku tahu, aku nak dengar jerit dia tu hari-hari

[Verse 2]
Cermin sisi kita cari kat kedai potong
Kusyen belakang dia jahit sendiri, benang lain warna
Ayah dia berdiri tepi pagar, tangan dalam poket
"Kalau rosak tengah jalan, jangan telefon pakcik"

[Pre-Chorus]
Petang tadi kita isi minyak
Sepuluh ringgit, cukup sampai pantai

[Bridge - drums drop to floor toms, guitar swells]
Radio tak jalan, tingkap kena engkol
Dia nyanyi sendiri, sumbang, kuat, aku ikut

[Chorus - full band, gang vocals]
Pusing kunci, sekali lagi
(Oh-oh, oh-oh)
Enjin batuk, enjin hidup
Tingkap turun, angin Port Dickson masuk
Dan aku tahu, aku nak bawa dia jalan macam ni hari-hari

[Outro - delay guitar alone]
Saga merah tu masih batuk, kita masih ketawa

tracks.title: Tarik Nafas Dulu
tracks.genre: Malay wedding pop (lagu kahwin akad nikah duet)
tracks.mood: sentimental, nervous and laughing at itself
tracks.subject: a groom whose lafaz sticks on the mas kahwin amount at the akad nikah until the tok kadi tells him to breathe, and the second try that makes it sah
tracks.caption: Malay wedding pop in the lagu kahwin akad nikah duet style. A kompang ensemble playing interlocking bertingkah patterns in the intro and outro like an arak pengantin procession, with rebana underneath; a nylon-string acoustic guitar picking through the verses; warm piano chords; a soft 4/4 kit played with brushes and rim clicks. Warm and roomy, the kompang forward only in the intro and outro, the two voices close and on top. A warm male-female duet, sentimental and unhurried, trading verses and singing the last chorus in unison. 96 BPM, A major. Sentimental, nervous and laughing at itself. No trap drums, no autotune, no EDM build, no dangdut beat, no power-ballad key change, no swelling string section, no nasyid choir harmonies, no lagu raya accordion.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - kompang bertingkah and nylon guitar]

[Verse 1 - Male]
Songkok baru, sampin pinjam abang ipar
Tok kadi genggam tangan aku, sejuk macam ais
Satu masjid senyap, kipas siling pun aku dengar
Lafaz aku tersangkut tengah jalan, kat angka mas kahwin

[Pre-Chorus - Female]
Dari belakang aku nampak telinga dia merah
Mak aku dah pegang tisu, abah aku pandang lantai

[Chorus - Duet]
Tok kadi senyum, "Tarik nafas dulu"
Sekali lagi, perlahan, satu-satu
Bila saksi angguk, "Sah"
Baru aku boleh bernafas

[Verse 2 - Female]
Petang tu atas pelamin, mak andam betulkan selendang
Dia bisik kat aku, "Malu, satu masjid gelak"
Aku kata, "Takpe, abang, cerita ni kita bawa sampai tua"
Video tu adik aku dah hantar dalam group keluarga

[Bridge - kompang falls away, guitar and piano]
Kalau abang tersangkut lagi satu hari nanti
Aku ada sebelah, aku ingatkan, tarik nafas dulu

[Chorus - Duet, in unison]
Tok kadi senyum, "Tarik nafas dulu"
Sekali lagi, perlahan, satu-satu
Kali kedua, suara tak goyang langsung
Dan satu masjid sebut "Sah" sama-sama

[Outro - kompang procession fading]
Arak pengantin, kompang di depan
Tarik nafas dulu, sayang

tracks.title: Tunggu Kamek Kat Tangga
tracks.mood: teasing, flirty and quick on its feet
tracks.subject: the drummer-singer behind the batik curtain teasing, in pantun, the young man from the next kampung who turns up every gendang night in his cousin's oversized shoes
tracks.caption: Sarawak Malay gendang music in the bermukun pantun-exchange style. The seh gendang, a seated female singer behind a batik curtain, plays the gendang hand drums herself, dry slaps and open booming strokes in a quick interlocking dance rhythm that drives every section; a biola violin opens with a short free-time phrase before the drums enter, then answers the voice between pantun lines; no chordal instrument at all, the drums and voices carry the song. Live and roomy like a village hall at night, the hand drums and voices forward, the violin a step behind. A bright, quick-witted female singer trading teasing pantun quatrains with a playful male voice, both conversational with laughter in the delivery, and a small group shouting the written replies. 112 BPM, G minor. Teasing, flirty and quick on its feet. No accordion, no drum kit, no electric bass, no joget or ronggeng lilt, no slow dondang sayang sway, no pop synths, no autotune.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - short free-time biola phrase, then the gendang enters]

[Verse 1 - Female drummer-singer]
Pergi ke pekan membeli tali,
Tali diikat di pokok nangka;
Kasut abang besar sekali,
Pinjam sepupu dari Mukah?

[Verse 2 - Male dancer answers]
Buah rambai di tepi titi,
Dimakan tupai dua biji;
Kasut longgar abang ikat mati,
Asal dapat dengar adik menyanyi.

[Chorus - Female, group answers]
Menandak, abang, menandak
(Menandak lagi!)
Kalau kasut tercabut, jangan lari balik
Gendang ni tak tunggu sesiapa

[Verse 3 - Female drummer-singer]
Kain batik digantung tinggi,
Tirai dipasang di tengah dewan;
Kasut abang tercampak ke kiri,
Jatuh ke dalam pinggan hidangan.

[Bridge - drums drop out, biola and voice]
Tirai ni nipis, abang, kamek nampak semua
Abang datang bukan sebab nak menandak pun

[Chorus - Female, group answers]
Menandak, abang, menandak
(Menandak lagi!)
Kasut sebelah pun tak apa
Lepas gendang, tunggu kamek kat tangga

[Outro - gendang alone, sudden stop]
Pulangkan kasut sepupu tu esok pagi!

[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.title: Jaga Durian
tracks.mood: rowdy, proud and half asleep
tracks.subject: three cousins on the night shift in a durian orchard hut in Kuala Pilah, racing each other in the dark to every thud
tracks.caption: Negeri Sembilan caklempong folk song in the Minangkabau gong-chime tradition. Rows of small bossed kettle-gongs, the handheld caklempong pacik and the rack-mounted caklempong duduk, playing bright interlocking melodic patterns; a double-headed gendang driving a quick dance rhythm; a low hanging gong struck at the end of each phrase; a bansi bamboo flute answering the vocal lines. Open-air and lively, the gong-chimes forward and ringing, the gendang punchy, voices dry. A bright male folk lead singing short lines with a grin in his voice, the ensemble shouting the written sorak replies. 128 BPM, G major. Rowdy, proud and half asleep. No drum kit, no electric guitar, no rock band, no synths, no accordion, no joget violin or 6/8 lilt, no dangdut beat, no autotune.

[Intro - caklempong interlocking pattern and gendang]

[Verse 1]
Musim durian, Kuala Pilah, malam Sabtu
Pondok buluh, lampu suluh, ubat nyamuk dua gelung
Den dengan Pian, dengan Adik Kecik
Tiga sepupu, satu termos kopi o

[Pre-Chorus]
Angin bertiup, dahan bergoyang
Semua diam, telinga panjang

[Chorus]
Gedebuk! Siapa dulu?

Lari dalam gelap, tersadung akar
Durian jatuh, tiga orang jatuh

[Verse 2]
Pukul dua, Pian dah berdengkur

tracks.caption: Malay mystic death metal in the old-Malay incantation style. Deep guttural male growls throughout, with a low spoken male voice reciting the old-Malay incantation in the breakdown. 180 BPM, B minor. Furious, sleepless and deadly serious. No clean sung chorus, no metalcore melodic hooks, no pop structure, no autotune, no synth pads, no 80s hard-rock solo.

tracks.caption: Malaysian shoegaze in the Kuala Lumpur scene style, sung in Malay. tracks.title: Musim Tengkujuh
tracks.mood: tender, unhurried and content
tracks.subject: a Terengganu fisherman's wife weaving songket at her loom through the monsoon while her husband, boat beached, mends the same net beside her
tracks.caption: Malay court gamelan song in the Terengganu gamelan Melayu tradition, adapted for voice. A keromong of small kettle-gongs playing a steady interlocking melody in a five-note gamelan tuning; a wooden gambang running soft quick patterns; saron kecil and saron besar metallophones carrying the main melody in slow even strokes; a gendang hand drum leading every change of tempo; kenong and a pair of large hanging gongs marking the end of each cycle. Warm and roomy like a wooden palace hall, the metallophones forward and ringing, the gongs deep and long, the voice close and plain. A soft, restrained female voice in a low-middle register, unornamented and unhurried, placed over the gong cycles. 72 BPM, D minor. Tender, unhurried and content. No drum kit, no electric bass, no piano, no pop strings or ballad chords, no Balinese gong kebyar shimmer, no autotune, no melismatic runs.

tracks.caption: Taiwanese Hokkien gangster-film brotherhood anthem with a cinematic hybrid score, half-time feel. tracks.title: 早頓店 Tsá-tǹg-tiàm
tracks.mood: playful bickering, twenty years in love
tracks.subject: a husband and wife who have run a breakfast shop for twenty years, she calling every customer 'handsome' at the counter while he grumbles at the griddle, until she finally calls him it
tracks.caption: Taiwanese Hokkien KTV duet over an upbeat swung two-step. A synth bass bouncing a two-step on root and fifth; a shuffled drum kit with a cross-stick backbeat; DX-style electric piano comping; clean chorus-effect guitar fills answering each vocal line; an alto sax playing the intro and interlude hook; the final chorus modulates up a whole step. Bright, clean karaoke-bar mix, both voices centred and forward, sax and guitar fills to the sides. A male baritone and a female soprano trading lines and teasing each other in the verses, harmonising in parallel thirds on the chorus. 104 BPM, F major. Playful bickering, twenty years in love. No sobbing enka delivery, no slow ballad tempo, no trap hi-hats, no autotune, no rap, no EDM drop.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse]
透早四點半 鐵板先燒
蛋餅 一塊一塊 煎甲赤赤
你徛佇櫃台 喙笑笑
逐个 攏喝「帥哥 欲食啥?」

[Verse]
你莫佇遐 咧食醋
彼个帥哥 七十八歲
做生理 喙就愛甜
你看 蛋餅閣煎甲臭火焦

[Pre-Chorus]
你逐个 攏叫帥哥
啊無 是欲叫啥?

[Chorus]
帥哥 欲食啥 免客氣
一个喝單 一个煎 二十冬矣
鐵板燒燒 奶茶甜甜
你的喙 比奶茶閣較甜

[Verse]
二十年前 你來買蛋餅
我煎甲臭火焦 你嘛食了了
是你 偷加我兩粒卵
閣無收錢 喝我「美女」

[Chorus]
帥哥 欲食啥 免客氣
一个喝單 一个煎 二十冬矣
鐵板燒燒 奶茶甜甜
臭火焦的 我嘛食二十冬

[Bridge]
其實彼工 看你看甲 袂記得翻面
其實 我叫遐濟帥哥 攏是咧練習叫你

[Chorus]
帥哥 欲食啥 免客氣
一个喝單 一个煎 二十冬矣
鐵板燒燒 奶茶甜甜
這聲帥哥 今仔日 是叫你

[Outro]
帥哥 欲食啥?
一份蛋餅 加兩粒卵

tracks.title: 濾水器 Lī-tsuí-khì
tracks.mood: furious, then dancing about it
tracks.subject: dressing up for coffee with a high-school crush who calls after ten years of silence, and dancing out of the café when he opens a water-purifier catalogue
tracks.caption: Taiwanese Hokkien electro dance-pop diva song, a choreographed verse-chorus pop song with an electro-house drop. A four-on-the-floor kick; a distorted saw bass in a pumping sidechain; a bright detuned square-wave synth riff carrying the main hook; claps on two and four; white-noise risers into a short instrumental drop after each chorus. Punchy, loud club mix, kick and lead vocal forward, synth riff wide. Commanding, bright female pop belt with spoken and shouted ad-libs, every hook sung live by the one voice. 128 BPM, E minor. Furious at the old classmate's sales pitch, then dancing about it. No festival truck-stage remix, no trap hi-hats, no autotune, no rap verse, no slow ballad section, no plaintive weeping.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse]
十年無消無息 你敲電話來
講欲約我 咖啡廳坐一下
我去做頭毛 閣畫目眉
穿我上媠 彼領紅洋裝

[Pre-Chorus]
你笑甲 喙齒白鑠鑠
對皮包 提出一本目錄

[Chorus]
你欲賣我濾水器 我就跳舞!
音樂 開予上大聲!
你講一句 我踏三步
這杯咖啡 我家己付!

[Verse]
你講 一台三萬六 分十二期
你講 揣兩个朋友 就會當趁錢
你講 我是你 上相信的人
十年來 這句上好笑

[Pre-Chorus]
你笑甲 喙齒白鑠鑠
閣提出 第二本目錄

[Chorus]
你欲賣我濾水器 我就跳舞!
音樂 開予上大聲!
你講一句 我踏三步
規間咖啡廳 攏咧看!

[Bridge]
我徛起來 共你講
十七歲 我寫予你的批
你一張 嘛無回
今仔日 我嘛無欲買

[Chorus]
你欲賣我濾水器 我就跳舞!
懸踏鞋 行出咖啡廳!
你講一句 我踏三步
十年暗戀 洗予清氣!

[Outro]
電話 閣響第二遍
我 攏無接
